newsitem.title: COMOROS: 45 survive crash of hijacked Ethiopia plane.
newsitem.headline: 45 survive crash of hijacked Ethiopia plane.

text.p: Forty-five people have so far been found alive after a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane came down in the sea off the Comoro Islands, a senior manager at Comoros airport said on Saturday.

"There are 45 survivors and they have found 50 bodies. Most of the survivors have been taken to hospitals but some are in local hotels," Ahmed Chanfe, deputy manager at the Comoros' main airport, said in a telephone interview.
Comoro Islands prime minister Tadjidine Ben Said Massoundi was due to make a statement on national radio, he said.

Airline officials said the pilot and one crew member were among those who survived when the plane, hijacked between Addis Ababa and its first scheduled stop in the Kenyan capital Nairobi, ran out of fuel and ditched while trying to land at Moroni airport.

Thirty bodies of crash victims, mostly Asians and Africans, were laid out under blankets in the conference room of a beach hotel near where the plane came down about 40 km (25 miles) north of Moroni, capital of the Indian Ocean archipelago.
